the_question_this_answers: gauge-layer-brief.md section 3 records that THE REVERSE-PHYSICS QUESTION HAS NEVER BEEN ASKED OF THE GAUGE STRUCTURE. For the action and the field equations the stream asked 'what is this equivalent to'; for the gauge layer it asked only 'is RP-DIFF independent', which is strictly weaker. The question worth asking is whether the gauge algebra Diff x Weyl is an ASSUMPTION or is FORCED by the action. This certificate answers it for the VECTOR-parameter half at bounded order. The SCALAR half was already settled by the generator count in REVERSE_PHYSICS_SYMBOLIC_FAMILY_V1: exactly ONE generator at curvature degree <= 2 over a COMPLETE ten-element candidate list.
establishes: that the vector-parameter sector of the gauge algebra of S = alpha int sqrt(-g) C^2 contains NO generator other than the DIFFEOMORPHISM one, at every derivative order up to and including THREE. Orders zero, one and three are computed; order two is EMPTY BY INDEX PARITY, and so is order four. Coverage in the coefficient's curvature degree differs by order and is stated per order rather than averaged: degree <= 2 at orders zero and one, degree 0 EXHAUSTIVELY at order three (enumerated, ranked, closed with a witness), and degree 1 at order three only by SAMPLING three structurally distinct candidates. The scalar sector is settled at degree <= 2, so together the gauge algebra at these orders is Diff x Weyl with nothing hidden -- a LOWER BOUND ON COMPLETENESS, reported as one.
how: Noether's second theorem makes gauge symmetries and Noether identities the same data. A local operator Delta_{mn}[xi] generates a gauge symmetry exactly when E^{mn} Delta_{mn}[xi] is a total divergence for every metric, equivalently when the adjoint vanishes identically. For a vector parameter at derivative order one, Delta_{mn}[xi] = S_{mn}^{rs} nabla_r xi_s has adjoint nabla_r (S_{mn}^{rs} E^{mn}). Writing W^r_s = S_{mn}^{ra} E^{mn} g_{as}, the condition is nabla_r W^r_s = 0 identically -- a covariant divergence of a rank-2 object, which is exactly the operation N1 already performs. The machinery is REUSED, not rebuilt: the same Bach tensor, the same cov_jets, the same symbolic metric family.
the_negatives_are_the_result: The two POSITIVE cases are already known and are recomputed only as premises: the Diff adjoint is N1 (nabla_r E^{rs} = 0) and the Weyl adjoint is N2 (the Bach trace). What makes 'exactly these' evidence rather than an enumeration that never ran is that curvature-weighted candidates MUST FAIL. Three were posed and all three fail: R times the Diff candidate, Ric contracted into the trace slot (the negative gauge-layer-brief.md names by hand, requiring B^{mn} Ric_{mn} = 0, which is not an identity), and Ric as a mixed factor. Liveness is checked before any of them, because every test here is satisfied by the zero tensor.
the_weyl_case_is_vacuous_and_says_so: The degree-zero Weyl candidate g_{mn} g^{rs} has adjoint nabla^s (tr E). The Bach tensor is TRACELESS, so tr E is identically zero and its gradient vanishes for that reason rather than independently. It is reported as REDUCING TO N2, not as a passing check. A vanishing-case control proves nothing, and this programme has now hit that failure mode repeatedly.
the_module_trap_sharpened: gauge-layer-brief.md warns that gauge symmetries form a module over FUNCTIONS, so g_{mn} R sigma is the Weyl generator reparametrised rather than a new symmetry, and a naive kernel dimension overcounts. The vector sector shows the trap is strictly worse than that. The degree-zero candidate g_{mn} g^{rs} gives Delta_{mn} = g_{mn} (nabla . xi), which is the Weyl generator with parameter sigma = nabla . xi -- a DIFFERENTIAL reparametrisation of the parameter, not a functional one. So the quotient must be by differential operators on the parameter, and a count that quotients only by function multiplication STILL OVERCOUNTS. The naive degree-zero kernel has three elements and the generator count is two.

order_two_is_empty_by_counting_indices: A coefficient at derivative order k in a vector parameter carries 2 + k + 1 indices. Every tensor built from the metric, its inverse, delta and UNDIFFERENTIATED curvature has EVEN rank: g and delta are rank 2, Ricci 2, Riemann 4, the scalar 0. So the odd-rank coefficient that even orders require cannot be built, and orders 0 and 2 are unreachable that way. The next possible order after one is THREE, not two.
and_why_order_zero_was_still_computed: The parity argument has a real limit, and it is the reason order zero was enumerated rather than dismissed with it: DERIVATIVES of curvature have ODD rank -- nabla_a R is rank 1, nabla_a R_{bc} is rank 3. So order zero IS reachable, with one derivative on the curvature in the coefficient. Two such candidates were posed and both come back nonzero, so there is no generator there either. Order zero is also the cheap sector: its adjoint is T_{mn}^{r} E^{mn} with no integration by parts, a CONTRACTION rather than a divergence.
triviality_is_excluded_by_construction: Every action has TRIVIAL gauge symmetries of the form Delta = M[E] with M antisymmetric under the exchange of its index pairs. They exist for any action, are infinite in number, and must not be counted. They are excluded here by construction rather than by assertion: every coefficient enumerated is built from the metric and curvature and never from E, and the Bach tensor is fourth order in the metric, so no candidate at this degree can contain it.
curvature_degree_two: Three structurally distinct candidates, not three variations on one: |Ric|^2 weighting the Diff candidate (a degree-2 SCALAR times the known generator), Ric^{r}{}_{m} Ric^{s}{}_{n} (both free indices carried by RICCI), and R^{r}{}_{m}{}^{s}{}_{n} (built from RIEMANN beyond its Ricci trace). All three come back NONZERO, so no generator hides at degree 2 either. THE RIEMANN-BUILT ONE IS THE POINT, and the scalar sector is why: its inherited seven-tensor list was built from g and Ric alone, and the candidates it OMITTED were exactly the ones contracting against Riemann -- an omission that was caught and cost a correction. E^{mn} for this action IS the Bach tensor, which sees the full Weyl tensor and not only its traces, so a Riemann-built candidate is precisely the kind that could carry a second generator. Leaving it out here would have repeated a known omission knowingly.
what_the_rank_prevented: Each of the three surviving contractions is separately nonzero, and reading that as 'no further symmetries at order three' would have been a wrong published claim. It is the same each-nonzero-is-not-independent confusion that already forced the cubic action count from 7 down to 5. The rank was computed by exact rational elimination precisely because of that precedent, and it caught it.
order_three_and_the_witness_that_settles: Order three is affordable because a degree-zero coefficient is COVARIANTLY CONSTANT and passes through the derivatives, so nabla^3(S E) = S . nabla^3 E and one third covariant derivative of the Bach tensor serves every candidate. Three POSITIVE CONTROLS hold: whenever the innermost derivative contracts with an index of B the innermost operation is div B, which N1 says is zero, and all three such contractions vanish identically through a rank-5 object. THE INTERESTING PART IS THE OTHER THREE. Each is separately NONZERO, but their base-point RANK is 2 of 3, which looks like a fourth symmetry. The vanishing combination is therefore EXHIBITED -- by carrying an identity through the elimination, the technique this certificate's cubic sibling uses -- and rebuilt on the FULL jets, where a real relation would have to be the zero polynomial at every outer order. IT IS NOT: one witness at the base point, ZERO verified identically. That decides it in the OPPOSITE direction to what the rank suggested. The base-point kernel is one-dimensional, spanned by that witness; any identically-vanishing combination would also vanish at the base point and so be proportional to it; the witness does not vanish identically; therefore none does. The true rank is EXACTLY 3 and the kernel is EXACTLY the three that vanish manifestly -- the contractions that vanish BECAUSE of N1 and N2, i.e. the differential reparametrisations of Diff and Weyl. Nothing new at order three, and the reparametrisation span never needed enumerating: the kernel is already exactly the set that vanishes for N1/N2 reasons.
the_methodological_point: This cuts both ways and both ways were live. The base-point rank of 2 was a FALSE ALARM -- an apparent degeneracy at one point rather than a real relation -- and reading it as exact would have invented a symmetry that is not there. Reading 'each of the three is nonzero' as sufficient would have reached the right answer for the WRONG REASON, which is the same confusion that forced the cubic action count from 7 to 5. A rank is a floor in one direction; a witness is what closes it in the other, and here it closes it by FAILING to verify.
order_three_with_curvature_in_the_coeffi: SAMPLED, NOT ENUMERATED, and the distinction is the point. The covariant-constancy shortcut that made degree zero cheap is gone: nabla S is not zero, the derivatives act on the coefficient too, and the adjoint must be taken of the PRODUCT. The naive route -- nabla^3 of the rank-4 product, n^7 jets at outer degree 7 -- was not attempted. Instead the divergence is taken at every step, since each derivative index meets an index of the object it differentiates and the innermost contracts first, so the rank never exceeds n^5: the same peak cost as degree zero with only the order of contraction changed. THE CONTROL IS THE DEGREE-ZERO ANSWER: run with the coefficient set to the constant 1, the new pipeline must reproduce what the covariantly-constant route already settled, and it does. A new pipeline is checked against the settled one before any new answer is read off it.
